_comment: Display names for the audit's signals. Identifiers (keys) are stable - they appear in config weights, stored audits and the API - only these labels are shown to users. A backend test keeps this file in sync with config.json.

llms_txt_exists.label: llms.txt file present
llms_txt_exists.check: A /llms.txt file exists at the domain root. It gives AI systems a guide to the site's most important content.

llms_txt_valid.label: llms.txt readable as text
llms_txt_valid.check: The llms.txt file is served as plain text or Markdown, not as an HTML page.

llms_txt_enriched.label: llms.txt well structured
llms_txt_enriched.check: The llms.txt file uses Markdown structure (headings, lists, bold text) so AI systems can parse it.

robots_txt_exists.label: robots.txt file present
robots_txt_exists.check: A /robots.txt file exists and can be read.

sitemap_exists.label: Sitemap available
sitemap_exists.check: A sitemap is declared in robots.txt, and a sitemap file can be fetched from the site.
sitemap_exists.scope: twice: declared in robots.txt, and file reachable

sitemap_type_valid.label: Sitemap structure valid
sitemap_type_valid.check: The sitemap is a recognised XML type (URL set or sitemap index), not an unknown or invalid one.

sitemap_freshness.label: Sitemap updated within 7 days
sitemap_freshness.check: The sitemap's last-modified dates are no older than one week.

ai_crawler_access.label: AI crawlers allowed
ai_crawler_access.check: robots.txt lets AI crawlers (for example GPTBot) fetch the site's pages.

search_crawler_access.label: Search crawlers allowed
search_crawler_access.check: robots.txt lets search-engine crawlers (for example Googlebot) fetch the site's pages.

site_scrapable.label: Pages can be crawled
site_scrapable.check: The site's pages could be fetched and read, and were not blocked by bot protection or hidden behind scripts.

canonical_exists.label: Canonical tag present
canonical_exists.check: The page names its preferred URL with a canonical tag.

canonical_matches.label: Canonical points to the page itself
canonical_matches.check: The canonical URL is the same as the page's own final URL.

canonical_clean.label: Canonical URL has no query parameters
canonical_clean.check: The canonical URL has no query string (such as ?utm_source=…), which would otherwise create duplicate versions of the page.

jsonld_exists.label: Expected structured data present
jsonld_exists.check: The JSON-LD schema types expected for this site type (for example Organization or Product) are present on the site.

jsonld_valid.label: Structured data valid
jsonld_valid.check: The JSON-LD found on the site passes validation for its schema type.

og_tags_exists.label: Open Graph tags present
og_tags_exists.check: The first page analysed carries Open Graph tags, which are used when links are shared or summarised.

og_tags_complete.label: Open Graph tags complete
og_tags_complete.check: The first page analysed has Open Graph title, description, image, type and URL.

twitter_card_exists.label: Twitter/X card tag present
twitter_card_exists.check: The first page analysed declares a twitter:card tag for link previews on X / Twitter.

page_indexable.label: Page allowed in search (no noindex)
page_indexable.check: The page is not marked noindex, so search and AI crawlers may include it.

cluster_presence.label: Cited in the topic
cluster_presence.check: The brand is cited in at least one question of the topic.

cluster_dominance.label: Not outnumbered in the topic
cluster_dominance.check: No compared brand is named in more answers than this brand in the topic. A topic where nobody is named counts as held.

prompt_citation.label: Cited for the question
prompt_citation.check: The brand is cited for the question: it appears in at least one of the question's two answers.
